content.content: 201: description: The pet owner was successfully added. content: application/json: schema: $ref: '#/components/schemas/Owner' 400: description: Bad request. content: application/json: schema: $ref: '#/components/schemas/ProblemDetail' 409: description: >- Conflict: the telephone number, email or household is already in use, or the owner's city already contains 50 or more owners. content: application/json: schema: $ref: '#/components/schemas/ProblemDetail' 429: description: Too many requests; 100 or more owners have already been created today. content: application/json: schema: $ref: '#/components/schemas/ProblemDetail' telephone: title: Telephone number description: >- The telephone number of the pet owner, stored and returned in E.164 form. Spaces, dashes and brackets are removed. A leading '+' and country code are kept; otherwise a single leading '0' is dropped and country code '+61' is assumed. Between 8 and 15 digits must follow the '+', e.g. '0412 345 678' is stored as '+61412345678'. Numbers with country code '+61' must have exactly 9 national digits and numbers with country code '+1' exactly 10. type: string minLength: 1 maxLength: 20 example: '+61412345678' email: title: Email address description: >- The optional email address of the pet owner. When present it must be a syntactically valid address; it is stored and returned lower-cased. type: string format: email maxLength: 255 example: 'george.franklin@example.com' registrationDate: title: Registration date description: >- The date the owner registered with the clinic. On create, when omitted it defaults to the server's current date. A Saturday or Sunday (supplied or defaulted) is rolled forward to the following Monday. type: string format: date example: '2020-06-15' sharesHousehold: title: Shares household description: >- Set to true on create to allow the owner even though another owner already has the same last name and address (compared case-insensitively with collapsed whitespace). Otherwise such a create is rejected with 409 Conflict. When true and such owners exist, the new owner joins their household and all of them share the same 'householdId'. content.text:
Duplicate detection now uses one derived `identityKey`, and a new owner gets a 409 only when its whole key equals an existing owner's. The full suite passes: 13 tests, 0 failures.

**How the key is built:** `normalizedTelephone|email|householdId`. A missing email or household becomes an empty string, and the email is lower-cased.
- **Exposed to clients:** the key is returned on the owner as `identityKey` and in the 409 response body.
- **Not stored:** it's computed on `Owner` (`Owner.getIdentityKey()`), so there's no schema change or backfill.
- **The check:** `ownerIdentityKeyExists` loads the owners with the same telephone and compares their full keys.

**What changed in behaviour:**
- **Removed checks:** the separate telephone, email and household duplicate checks are gone, along with their three exception classes, error handlers, and the repository/service methods only they used.
- **Same telephone or same email alone** is no longer a duplicate.
- **Same last name and address** is no longer rejected. `sharesHousehold` now only decides whether the new owner joins the household.
- **Household members** with different telephones are both allowed. The same telephone is also allowed when one owner is in a household and the other isn't.

**Order of steps in `addOwner`:** the new owner joins the household first, because that's when it gets the householdId that goes into the key. The duplicate check runs after that. I made `addOwner` `@Transactional`, so if the create is then rejected (duplicate, city capacity or daily limit), the household change is rolled back. `deleteOwner` already uses `@Transactional` in the same controller.

**Two things to be aware of:**
- **Joining can itself cause a 409.** When a new owner joins, the existing members get the same householdId. So if the newcomer has the same telephone and email as a member, the full keys match and it's rejected. One of my own tests first assumed this would be allowed; I rewrote that test because the 409 follows the spec.
- **Updates aren't checked.** The spec only covers new owners, so `updateOwner` doesn't check `identityKey`.

I added 8 tests to `AcceptanceTest.java` (no clash on the same telephone with a different email, or the same email with a different phone, household cases, key format, 409 body) and updated `openapi.yml` to match.

**What changed in behaviour:**
- **Removed checks:** the separate telephone, email and household duplicate checks are gone, along with their three exception classes, error handlers, and the repository/service methods only they used.
- **Same telephone or same email alone** is no longer a duplicate.
- **Same last name and address** is no longer rejected. `sharesHousehold` now only decides whether the new owner joins the household.
- **Household members** with different telephones are both allowed. The same telephone is also allowed when one owner is in a household and the other isn't.

**Order of steps in `addOwner`:** the new owner joins the household first, because that's when it gets the householdId that goes into the key. The duplicate check runs after that. I made `addOwner` `@Transactional`, so if the create is then rejected (duplicate, city capacity or daily limit), the household change is rolled back. `deleteOwner` already uses `@Transactional` in the same controller.

**Two things to be aware of:**
- **Joining can itself cause a 409.** When a new owner joins, the existing members get the same householdId. So if the newcomer has the same telephone and email as a member, the full keys match and it's rejected. One of my own tests first assumed this would be allowed; I rewrote that test because the 409 follows the spec.
- **Updates aren't checked.** The spec only covers new owners, so `updateOwner` doesn't check `identityKey`.

I added 8 tests to `AcceptanceTest.java` (no clash on the same telephone with a different email, or the same email with a different phone, household cases, key format, 409 body) and updated `openapi.yml` to match.
